newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metal mostly higher, PGMs soar again.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metal mostly higher, PGMs soar again.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were mostly higher early Monday, except for gold, with platinum group metals (PGMs) posting new contracts highs on the open and palladium fuutures locked limit up for the second day in row.

"Unlike Friday when there were only a few lots done, today palladium is limit bid for several hundred lots and with more shortcovering to come it could be like this for a couple more days," RJ Futures floor trader Ralph D'Esposito said.
NYMEX September palladium was up $9.00 at $215.60 an ounce, a new contract high, while December palladium was also up the expanded second-day limit of $9.00 at 207.60, also a new contract high.
NYMEX October platinum was up $8.00 at $446.50 an ounce, after seeing a new contract high early at $447.90.
PGM futures surged even higher on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) overnight, with all palladium contracts going limit up for the fourth day in a row, as heavy shortcovering continued.

No further Russian shipments of platinum group metals (PGMs) are expected in Japan under the annual supply contract until around August 10, and offerings earlier this week by Russia in the spot market of parcels of only about 15,000 ounces of platinum are not meeting demand, traders said.
COMEX September silver was up 1.5 cents at $4.485 an ounce, after fund buying pushed the contract to its highest level since July 7, above $4.50 an ounce, setting off some stop orders, traders said.
But back months in silver were lower.
But COMEX December gold was down $1.00 an ounce at $327.90, with support now seen around $327.30 and then $326.00.

The CFTC Commitment of Traders data, released late Friday, for the period ended July 29, showed funds had reduced their net short COMEX gold positions to 56,626 contracts from a near record 74,588 contracts two weeks earlier.
In the bullion market spot gold, was quoted $323.70/20 early, compared with the London Monday morning fix at $324.05 and the New York close Friday at $324.40/90.

But gold and silver are still seen capped by a further rise in the U.S. dollar overnight to new seven year highs against the mark, new four year highs against the Swiss franc, and a new seven year high on the dollar's trade weighted index.
